correctness.evidence: Independent replay and exact-arithmetic reconstruction support the finite headline claims. The committed verifier reports 136 isolating disks and verifies the Rouche inequalities at r=3/10 and r=1/100, pairwise disjointness by degree, the maximal-real-part separation, and the Szego-gap separation. The audit independently reconstructed m=|a1|r-|a0|>M and |a0|<|a1|r in exact Fraction arithmetic for all 136 disks at both radii. Exact disjointness plus one Rouche-counted zero per disk and n disks for degree n accounts for all zeros for 1<=n<=16. The maximal-real-part witness has lower bound 7.716102197 while every competitor has upper bound at most 6.984780933; the Szego-gap witness upper bound 0.161927324 is below every competing lower bound, at least 0.170167940. Residual implementation risks noted in AUDIT.json do not affect those finite claims.

originality.evidence: The checked prior literature concerns asymptotic location, limit curves, and expository treatment of zeros of exponential partial sums. The existing literature search and comparison did not identify the same finite certified package: 136 per-zero disjoint rational Rouche disks for 1<=n<=16, replayable one-zero counts, whole-disk Szego-gap enclosures, and the two finite-scope extremal witnesses. The originality finding is deliberately narrow: no new limit theorem or asymptotic theory is claimed; the contribution is the certified, replayable small-n table and its finite extremal data.

scientific_value.evidence: The record converts ordinary floating-point zero approximations into exact, replayable finite certificates for a canonical family of exponential sections. The isolation disks, count proofs, and extremal witnesses provide reproducibility and validation benchmarks for numerical root-finding, stability-region calculations, and experiments around the Szego curve. The scope n<=16 is modest, but the result is concrete, independently checkable, and useful as reference data rather than an arbitrary parameter sweep.

decision: Validated: all three axes pass within the stated finite scope. Correctness is supported by replayable exact certificates; originality is limited to the certified small-n data/certificate layer and finite extremal witnesses; scientific value is as a reproducible benchmark and reference dataset.
